candidate.question_text: A counter uses base five and currently displays 34. One more item is added. What should the display show?
candidate.explanation: Base five has digits 0 to 4. Adding one to the units digit 4 makes zero units and carries one group of five, so 34 becomes 40.

candidate.question_text: Two decimal labels are 404 and 440. A learner says the zeros have the same effect because both numbers contain two 4s. Which comparison is correct?

options.text: They are equal because both digit sums are 8.
404 is 36 greater.
440 is 36 greater because a 4 has moved from units to tens.
440 is 4 greater because it ends in zero.

candidate.explanation: In 404, the final 4 contributes 4. In 440, the middle 4 contributes 40. Their difference is 40 - 4 = 36.

candidate.question_text: A class has 40 pupils. On Monday 75% attend; on Tuesday 80% attend. How many more pupils attend on Tuesday?
candidate.explanation: Monday attendance is 30 and Tuesday attendance is 32. A rise of 5 percentage points is 5% of 40, or 2 pupils.

options.text: 2400 divided by 0.80

candidate.explanation: The reduced price is 80% of the original price, so divide 2400 by 0.80 to get Rs 3000. Adding 20% of the reduced price uses the wrong base.

candidate.question_text: A shop buys a model for Rs 800 and sells it for Rs 920. A learner divides the Rs 120 gain by Rs 920 to find profit percent. Which correction is right?

options.text: Divide by the cost price Rs 800 to get 15%.
Divide by Rs 120 to get 100%.
Subtract 15% from Rs 920.
The profit is 120%, since the gain is Rs 120.

candidate.explanation: Profit percent compares the gain with the cost price: 120/800 x 100 = 15%. The selling price is not the denominator.

candidate.question_text: A right-angled support has hypotenuse 26 cm and one perpendicular side 10 cm. A learner subtracts 10 from 26 and gets 16 cm for the other side. What is the other side?

options.text: 16 cm
36 cm
24 cm
28 cm

candidate.explanation: Subtract the squared lengths, then take the square root: 26 squared - 10 squared = 576, so the unknown side is 24 cm.

candidate.question_text: A rectangle measures 8 m by 15 m. A cable runs along its diagonal with no slack. How much shorter is it than following two adjacent edges between the same opposite corners?

options.text: 6 m

candidate.explanation: The diagonal is 17 m because 8 squared + 15 squared = 17 squared. Two adjacent edges total 23 m, so the saving is 6 m.

candidate.question_text: A learner cuts six equal square faces for a cube net but has not chosen how to join them. Which statement is justified?

options.text: Any arrangement of six joined squares must fold into a cube.
Six equal squares are the right faces, but their arrangement must also fold without overlap.
A cube net must contain exactly one triangular face.
The squares must all be different sizes.

candidate.explanation: A net must fold into the solid. Having the correct faces is necessary, but an unsuitable arrangement can make faces overlap or leave the solid unclosed.

candidate.question_text: A line graph records a tank at 20 L at 9 AM, 35 L at 10 AM and 30 L at 11 AM. Which statement is supported by these readings alone?

options.text: The tank lost 5 L from 9 AM to 11 AM.
The tank gained exactly 15 L during every hour.
The tank had a net gain of 10 L from 9 AM to 11 AM.
The tank could never have overflowed between readings.

candidate.explanation: The last reading minus the first is 30 - 20 = 10 L. The three readings do not determine everything that happened between them.

candidate.question_text: In a three-level number pyramid, each box is the sum of the two boxes below it. The bottom row is 3, x, 8 and the top is 25. Which equation finds x?
candidate.explanation: The middle boxes are 3 + x and x + 8. Adding them gives 3 + 2x + 8 = 25, so x appears twice.

candidate.question_text: Each box in a three-level number pyramid is the sum of the two boxes below it. Only the middle number in the bottom row increases by 2. What happens to the top number?

options.text: It rises by 2.
It stays unchanged.
It falls by 2.
It rises by 4 because the changed number contributes through both middle-row boxes.

candidate.explanation: Writing the bottom row as a, b, c gives top a + 2b + c. Replacing b by b + 2 adds 4 to the top, not 2.

candidate.question_text: A baker uses the same dough recipe twice. Dough with living yeast rises; dough without yeast does not. Which explanation fits the yeast treatment?

options.text: Yeast creates extra flour from nothing.
The dough rises only because yeast is a solid.
Yeast activity releases gas that forms spaces in the dough.

candidate.question_text: The same toy car is released from the same ramp height onto two level surfaces. It stops sooner on the rough surface. Which explanation is consistent with friction?

options.text: The rough surface creates only a non-contact force.
The contact force from the rough surface opposes the car's motion more strongly.
Friction always pushes a moving car forward.
A level surface cannot exert friction.

candidate.explanation: Friction is a contact force that opposes motion or attempted motion between surfaces. With other conditions held similar, the earlier stop on the rough surface is consistent with stronger friction.

candidate.question_text: The same loaded bag rests first on a 0.04 square metre face and then on a 0.02 square metre face. Its weight is unchanged. What happens to the pressure on the floor?

options.text: It doubles.

It stays the same.
It becomes zero.

candidate.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area. With the same force and half the contact area, pressure doubles.

candidate.question_text: A model has neighbouring regions of relatively high and low air pressure. Which direction of airflow is consistent with pressure differences?

options.text: Low pressure to high pressure in every case.

candidate.explanation: A pressure difference drives air from a region of higher pressure towards lower pressure. This is the basic model; it does not mean every real wind follows an uncurved path.

candidate.question_text: Two solutions each contain 100 mL water at the same temperature. A has 5 g dissolved sugar and B has 15 g, with all sugar dissolved. Which statement follows?

options.text: A has more dissolved sugar per equal amount of water.
B must be saturated.

candidate.question_text: A class records a sequence of Moon shapes: thin crescent, half, then more than half illuminated. Which next research step would test whether the pattern repeats?

options.text: Watch an unrelated star for one minute.
Assume the sequence proves the Moon makes its own light.
Continue dated Moon observations over several weeks and compare the sequence.

candidate.explanation: A repeating cycle is tested by observations across enough time to see whether the pattern returns. Three drawings alone do not establish the whole cycle or show that the Moon produces its own light.
